key_insight: Graph grounding reduces hallucinations across evaluated LLMs, while general-purpose models generally lead on multi-hop and high-level reasoning.
engineering_relevance: Pair broad-capability LLMs with structured domain knowledge, selecting integration strategies according to reasoning complexity and computational constraints.
method: Benchmark five LLMs: GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, and BioGPT.
Evaluate across DrugBank, NeuroSynth, Cognitive Atlas, Brain Map, and GDPKG.
Compare graph-grounded and graph-agnostic conditions using multitier queries.
evidence_signal: The benchmark reports substantial annotation agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.781; Fleiss’ κ = 0.77), declining performance with query complexity, and reduced hallucinations with graph grounding.
watch_item: The abstract provides no effect sizes or runtime costs, limiting assessment of grounding’s practical accuracy–compute trade-off.
paper_title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
